_what: Settings of the record store (src/storage/record_store/), read once by settings.rs. receipts: how long and how many request receipts each record's current row keeps (a retry inside them is answered with its first change; outside them compare-and-set still refuses a second apply). undo_window_ms: how long replaced versions, tombstones and destroyed records stay (history readable, destruction restorable only by the operator) before the exit step removes them physically; must be at least the receipt window. exit_step_rows: the most rows one exit step removes per family (each write runs one step, and a host timer may run more). reclaim_step_pages: the most pages (4 KiB each) one reclaim step gives back to the volume after removals (RecordStore::reclaim_step, run by the account's owner between requests, never inside one), so a step holds the store for a few milliseconds and an erasure never waits on a rewrite of the file. kind_field: the top-level text field naming a record's kind, which the live_kind order lists by. search: the search port's layout and the top-level text fields it reads; the shipped layout is segments (src/storage/record_store/segments.rs): changes wait in memory, a write persists them as one packed segment at flush_records records or when the oldest is flush_seconds old, parts are about part_bytes, and fan_in segments of one level merge into the next (the simulation's daily-segments winner: +0.11 rows per create, about 18 rows per search, a cold start bounded by the unflushed tail). A write never merges: merges run in the account's idle upkeep (segments.rs search_merge), each step reading about merge_bytes of input parts and committed alone, so a write's time does not grow with the index (the old application record-log-store.mjs, the same index merge in resumable turns of at most 4 MiB, because one merge done at once held a 4 GB store for 4 to 12 seconds). walk_rows: the records one step of the search walk reads (segments.rs search_walk, the old application record-log-store.mjs buildIndexes): a scope that held rows before its index or its current terms existed is walked in id order, a page per idle upkeep step, its frontier and cursor kept beside the segments in search_walk, so a stopped walk starts where it left off. orders: declared field orders (src/storage/record_store/orders.rs): each names the record kind it covers and the path of the field it orders by (a step into a string holding JSON reads the JSON inside it); the store keeps one ordered row per covered record, written on create, rewritten only when the ordered value changes and removed with the record, so a page in that order is one range scan plus one get per record shown. totals: declared totals (src/storage/record_store/totals.rs): each names the record kind it adds up, an optional group field and an optional integer sum field; the store keeps one row per account, total and group, changed in the same write as the record, so every total of an account is one range scan; a total counts the records written while it is declared, so it is declared before its kind is first written. computer_record_bytes is the largest record value a store of a computer keeps. one_item_page_bytes: a page holds items up to records::MAX_PAGE_BYTES (4 MiB); one item larger than that is answered as a page of its own, up to this many bytes as JSON, the way the old application carried a row larger than a page (src/resource-state-carry.mjs:11 ROW_BYTES, 16 MiB, and :322-328): a record of up to computer_record_bytes, with what travels with it, is never refused by the page that carries it. settle: the bounds of record sync (src/storage/record_store/record_sync.rs, the old application record-sync.mjs): most_rows log rows and about bytes bytes of net changes per answer or upload (the old application 5,000 rows and 4,000,000 characters; 4 MiB here), upload_rows envelopes per upload batch (the old application PAGE 200), bucket_page_records records per bucket page (the old application 500), verify_buckets buckets read and checked together, and record_bytes the largest single envelope that still crosses alone in its own message when it is past bytes (the old application resource-state-carry: a row up to 16 MiB goes as its own page); past it a settle refuses (413). settle_mirror: whether every write of a store whose owner did not choose also makes its records into the settle store of its scope in the same transaction (mod.rs mirror_settle). The copies choose it for every store they open (RecordStore::mirrored), so the account's replicated records are their settle store and a settle compares and catches them up; any other store keeps only its own rows (one row per create plus its orders), so this is false. A computer's byte budget is not here: each computer reports its own storage figure (src/account/computers.rs ComputerReport), either {"bytes": N} or {"keep_free_bytes": N} (what the store holds at open plus its volume's free bytes above N); the store refuses a change that leaves it larger.

holders._why: The writer's match index for a vault's replaced versions (record_store/holders.rs). A holder whose last pull is older than lease_ms is expired and stops holding the prune back. A holder behind the writer whose last pull is older than lag_ms is behind past the bound and stops holding it back; it gets a full copy when it returns.

undo_windows._why: How long a replaced version stays before the exit step may remove it, per profile (the resource row's `undo`). records: 30 days. vault: 1 day, so a put that overwrote a good secret can be undone for a day (the re-key loss, 2026-11).

vacuum._why: The one-time full vacuum that makes a store file incremental auto-vacuum, so its free pages go back in reclaim_step steps with no further rewrite (storage/sqlite.rs reclaim; old trillion never gave a file's free pages back). A store's file is vacuumed once when its free pages are at least free_fraction of its pages, the volume has at least free_disk_factor times the file's size free, and the store has been idle for idle_ms (no commit in that window). The Mac's 3.6 GB vault qualifies once its legacy versions drain (PR #362, #412).

totals._why: files_summary of the account files (src/account_files/mod.rs): files and bytes per store, the Worker's account_files_summary_origins.
files_summary of the account files: every name, across the per-folder name scopes.
files_summary of the account files: chunks and their bytes.
files_summary of the account files: uploads in progress and their declared bytes.

_page_bytes_why: The page size a new store file starts with (src/storage/record_store_resources.rs open; a file that already has pages keeps its own). A WITHOUT ROWID row keeps at most (page - 12) * 64 / 255 - 23 bytes in its leaf and spills the rest to overflow pages of its own: 1,002 bytes at 4 KiB, so each record over about 1 KB took a fresh, mostly empty 4 KiB overflow page (7.79 GB of them in the 34.6 GB primary book, storage audit 2026-11-03); at 32 KiB a row keeps 8,199 bytes in its leaf. Measured by src/storage/record_store/page_tests.rs on a synthetic copy of 100,000 records (log-normal, mean 1.8 KB, median 1.3 KB; raw values 181.6 MB) on November 3, 2026: bytes on disk 377.5 MB at 4 KiB, 388.6 MB at 8 KiB, 322.6 MB at 16 KiB, 258.6 MB at 32 KiB (31.5% less), 237.2 MB at 64 KiB. 32 KiB is chosen over 64 KiB because an empty store is 480 KiB rather than 960 KiB and each written page is half the size, for 8% fewer bytes.

store_size._what: How big one store may grow, ported one to one from the old application src/store-size.json (555926aa57, b3be01b859), read by src/storage/record_store/store_size.rs for every record store. A store's row is the account's plan or contract row when it has one, else the computer's own row (src/account/computers.rs ComputerReport store_size), else `default` (the old application's numbers). A level is reached at its share of limit_bytes, or within its headroom_bytes of it; the highest level reached is the store's level. Adding a level, or changing a number, is a row here or in the computer's or the account's row, never code.

default._why: Temporary containment 2026-11-12 4:50 AM CST: the local write outbox (8.86 GB, never pruned) crossed refuse-growth under the decided 10,000,000,000-byte ceiling (constraint decimal-cap, decision-lane-2, accepted by the person). Restored to 10 GiB until the D50 outbox prune lands; then set back to 10,000,000,000. the person, 2026-11-03: unlimited small stores, never one everything-store; a computer or an account's plan or contract may give another row.

levels._why: Writes still succeed: the store is reported and its history leaves faster (history.from_level), so it is freed long before anything is refused (the old application src/store-size.json:10; agreed 2026-10-16, it was 0.8).

Work that only adds (new runs, copies, caches) is refused here, or lands in the next store (volume_stores), so the space left serves the person's own writes and the store's recovery (the old application src/store-size.json:16).

A write fails once the pages it needs are not free, which is before the count reaches the limit; within this many bytes of the limit, calls wait for verified recovery first (the old application src/store-size.json:22, 2026-10-14).

store_size._growth_operations_why: The commands of an account's own records that only add (new runs, files taken in, imported or duplicated rows), refused before they keep anything once their store is at a level that refuses growth; every other command, the person's own writes among them, goes through (the old application src/store-size.json:5).

volume_stores._what: Which commands of an account's own records are volume: they add records without bound, so they land in a further store when the one they fill reaches next_store_at (store_size levels). Everything else stays in the primary store. Ported one to one from the old application own-record-volume.json (46485cba04); read by src/storage/record_store_resources/books.rs Books.
volume_stores._overflow_why: A further store is the primary's sibling named by its order (overflow:1, overflow:2; its file is the primary's name with .overflow-1, .overflow-2), so a second ask for the same next store names the same one.

full_store._what: What a store does once it is full (src/storage/record_store/full_store.rs), ported one to one from the old application src/full-store-recovery.mjs: a write at a level that waits for recovery (store_size) runs the store's recovery first; it frees only derived or expired space, one bounded page per step, never a real record; one recovery at a time per store; a recovery that freed nothing is not asked again for idle_ms (the old file's IDLE_MS, 60,000), so a store full of real records answers at once.

per_arrival._what: The per-arrival growth guard, ported one to one from the old application src/reliability-ceilings.json:34-46 `month` and test/store-month.test.mjs: a store lives through a simulated month (days of arrivals_per_day arrivals, the clock moving between them and the store's exit step running as its timer would), and what it keeps once it has sat quiet for settle_hours is at most database_bytes_per_arrival live bytes per arrival, with the month's last week no costlier per arrival than its first times late_growth_ratio (plus 64 bytes). seed makes the month's words the same every run. Read only by src/storage/record_store/month_tests.rs. The old file's request, wake and boot read ceilings and the bucket ceiling are not ported: this store reads by bounded pages (Work) and keeps no bucket.

_shared_children_why: Old trillion eeaf-sqlite-store.mjs contentId, per kind: each row {kind, fields} names top-level fields of that kind whose object value is stored once by its content identity (src/storage/record_store/shared.rs) and linked from every record holding it. No kind is named, so no record shares until its DATA names one.
_referrer_parts_why: Old trillion record-model.mjs partsOf and record-log-store.mjs holderKey/holdersOf: each row {kind, role, path, each?, role_from?, id_prefix?, absolute_prefix?, absolute_only?} names a field where records of that kind point to other records, kept in the kept_holders index so what holds a record is one range (src/storage/record_store/referrers.rs). No kind is named, so nothing is indexed until its DATA names one.
_referrers_walk_rows_why: Old trillion record-log-store.mjs MODEL_PAGE: one step of the walk that indexes records kept before their kind named its parts reads at most this many of the kind's records, and writes their holder keys and its cursor together.
_erase_with_why: Old trillion record-model.json erase_with, per kind: each row {kind, with: [{id: template} | {field: path} | {kind, order, equal?}]} names the records erased together with one record of that kind (src/storage/record_store/cascade.rs erase_cascading), in one write scope. No kind is named, so an erase takes only the record asked until its DATA names one.

keep._what: How a keep rule's row is read (src/storage/record_store/keep.rs): the rules kind (`rule_kind`, the person's list of rules, in the same store as the records the rules keep) and the column each part of a rule is in (`fields`): which kind of record (`kind`), when a record of it has expired (`expire_when`, the formula engine's rule tree and its fields, read over the record's own values and the fact `age_fact`, how long ago its newest write was, in milliseconds), how many records one firing destroys (`page`) and looks at (`walk`), and whether the rule is on (`enabled`: the choice `on_word`, or JSON true). When a rule runs is the person's own wake declaration (src/wake.rs), whose run asks the engine to apply a rule by id; no number of a rule, and no moment, is here.

history_archive._why: Old trillion src/record-history.json, per resource: replaced versions of a resource named in resources move out as chained JSONL files in the account's own files (folder) before they leave the store, rows_per_file and about bytes_per_file a file, once older than keep_ms; a history pin holds every version from its stamp on. No resource is named here, so no store archives until its DATA names a resource ("*" names every resource).

history._what: How long replaced versions stay in a store, bounded by bytes as well as by time, ported from the old application src/record-history.json:4 (history stays in the database for keep_ms, 1 hour, then leaves it). Below from_level a store keeps replaced versions for the undo window (undo_window_ms). Once the store reaches from_level (a share of its store_size row's limit), replaced versions older than keep_ms leave at once, rows_per_step per write, and full_store_rows_per_step once it reaches the level that waits for recovery. Old trillion moved them to chained files; here they leave the store (a file mover is not ported yet).
